entries.105668dee719a2de: A category covering the IT and Suica business, including credit card business, information processing business, power generation business and construction consulting business, among others. The company notes it as a business segment and similar not included in the reportable segments. Included are View Card Co., Ltd., JR East Mechatronics Co., Ltd., JR East Information Systems Co., Ltd., JR East Energy Development Co., Ltd., JR East Consultants Co., Ltd., UQ Communications Inc., and Central Security Patrol Co., Ltd. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, external customer revenue was ¥109,477 million (up 6.8% year on year), and segment profit (operating profit) was ¥30,274 million (up 32.0% year on year), the highest growth rate among the segments; segment assets were ¥1,482,114 million and the number of employees was 5,141. The company explains the revenue increase as higher sales related to the IC card business, and says it promoted 'Going Beyond Suica's Everyday Standards ~Suica Renaissance~' toward expanding Suica usage scenarios and evolving Suica into a daily life device. The company carried out linkage between 'Welcome Suica Mobile' and 'JR-EAST Train Reservation', introduced Suica on Shinano Railway, and conducted a demonstration test of walk-through ticket gates on the Joetsu Shinkansen.

entries.2083ea8ce1e475e8: The company operates conventional lines with an operating distance of 6,108.0 km. In the railway business revenue results of the company (the filing company), which are shown separately for the Kanto area and other areas, passenger transport revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,163,985 million in the Kanto area (up 3.9% year on year) and ¥67,074 million outside the Kanto area (up 2.8%). Passenger-kilometers were 99,232,608 thousand passenger-km in the Kanto area (up 3.1% year on year) and 5,295,189 thousand passenger-km outside the Kanto area (down 0.8%), and the passenger load factor for conventional lines overall is 43.6%. The company says it worked to improve transport quality, including measures against chronic delays on the Nambu Line, and advanced discussions with local municipalities along the lines toward building a sustainable transport system for regional local lines. The company is also advancing the installation of platform doors and other facilities using the railway station barrier-free fare system.

entries.271e347242ac3956: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥414,258 million, up 9.9% year on year, and the ratio to operating revenue was 13.4% (13.0% in the previous year). Operating expenses were ¥2,670.4 billion (up 6.4% year on year), of which operating costs of transportation and cost of sales were ¥1,952.8 billion and selling, general and administrative expenses were ¥717.5 billion. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥194,414 million for the Transportation Business, ¥128,252 million for the Real Estate and Hotel Business, ¥68,072 million for the Distribution and Services Business, ¥30,274 million for Other, and an adjustment of −¥6,755 million. Non-operating expenses rose to ¥91.2 billion due to higher interest paid and other factors, and ordinary profit was ¥351,645 million (up 9.4% year on year). Extraordinary income was ¥80.3 billion, mainly from higher gains on sales of investment securities, and extraordinary losses were ¥97.9 billion, mainly from recording a loss on revision of retirement benefit plans associated with the revision of personnel and wage systems, and profit attributable to owners of parent was ¥247,846 million (up 10.5% year on year). Impairment losses on fixed assets were ¥15,185 million, of which ¥9,111 million was in the Real Estate and Hotel Business. Net cash provided by operating activities was ¥765.0 billion, net cash used in investing activities was ¥877.6 billion, and free cash flow was an outflow of ¥112.5 billion. Interest-bearing debt at the end of the period was ¥5,162.2 billion, net interest-bearing debt after deducting cash and cash equivalents was ¥4,900.1 billion, and EBITDA (operating profit plus depreciation) was ¥842.9 billion. Long-term unpaid railway facility purchase payments related to Shinkansen railway facilities total ¥302.0 billion, payable by September 30, 2051 at a fixed annual interest rate of 6.55%.

entries.3e12f12747875767: The company and its affiliated companies (139 subsidiaries and 70 associates, as of March 31, 2026) operate the Transportation Business, the Retail and Service Business, the Real Estate and Hotel Business, and other businesses. The reportable segments are the first three, and Other is a category not included in the reportable segments. For the 39th fiscal period, there were 76 consolidated subsidiaries and 11 equity-method affiliates. The foundation is railways: the company's railway business mainly spans one metropolis and 16 prefectures in the Kanto and Tohoku regions, with 1,632 stations and a route length of 7,302.2 km (conventional lines 6,108.0 km, Shinkansen 1,194.2 km). It is a structure that connects the flow of people gathering there to in-station stores, shopping centers at and along stations, office buildings, hotels, and Suica. In July 2025 the company announced a new group management vision, "Yūshō 2034", placing "safety" as the top priority of group management, and set out two-axis management of "Mobility" (Transportation Business) and "Living Solutions" (Retail and Service Business, Real Estate and Hotel Business, and other businesses). On safety, under the "Group Safety Plan 2028", it targets zero accidents causing death or injury to customers and zero fatal accidents involving employees. For fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2031, it plans total investment of ¥6.6 trillion, and in addition to growth funds and funds for maintaining and strengthening the foundation, it has newly established "LX funds" for innovation. In July 2026, it plans an organizational restructuring that changes its three-tier structure of frontline workplaces, headquarters and branch offices, and head office into a two-tier structure of business headquarters, which integrate frontline workplaces with headquarters and branch offices, and head office. No single external customer accounts for 10% or more of consolidated operating revenue, and because revenue from external customers in Japan exceeds 90% of revenue, information by region is not disclosed.

entries.607295eedbbc1ff4: The company operates the Tohoku, Joetsu, Hokuriku, Yamagata and Akita Shinkansen lines. In the railway business revenue results of the company (the filing company), Shinkansen passenger transport revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥617,477 million (commuter pass ¥25,426 million, non-commuter ¥592,051 million), up 5.9% year on year. The operating distance is 1,194.2 km, passenger-kilometers were 23,735,947 thousand passenger-km (up 4.7% year on year), and the passenger load factor is 62.5%. The company says it worked on the 'Tsubasa, Tsunagu.' project to boost the Yamagata Shinkansen, which is being replaced by the new E8 series trains, and on promoting the appeal of the Hokuriku area through the 'Japanese Beauty Hokuriku' campaign. Under the train cargo transport service 'Hakobyun', the company began operating cargo-only Shinkansen trains.

entries.7bf2e47881fc6fd6: A category in which real estate for shopping centers, office buildings and hotels is developed and sold, handled by the company itself, JR East Real Estate Co., Ltd., and JR East Building Tech Co., Ltd. The company says it is accelerating its real estate turnover business (a business in which developed real estate is sold to recover funds for the next development), and in the fiscal year ended March 2026, higher real estate sales contributed to revenue growth.
entries.819142c48e76ca38: A reportable segment engaged in the shopping center operation business, the leasing of office buildings and others, the hotel business, and the real estate development and sales businesses that develop these, among others. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, external customer revenue was ¥513,227 million, exceeding that of the Distribution and Services Business and second only to the Transportation segment. Up 15.2% year on year, the fastest growth among the 3 reportable segments; segment profit (operating profit) was ¥128,252 million, segment assets were ¥2,765,681 million and the number of employees was 6,007. Capital expenditure was ¥454.3 billion, exceeding that of the Transportation segment, and was invested in construction work on TAKANAWA GATEWAY CITY, OIMACHI TRACKS, Shibuya Scramble Square and others. The company cites higher real estate sales, office rental income, and higher sales at shopping centers and hotels as reasons for the revenue increase, and says the grand opening of TAKANAWA GATEWAY CITY and the town opening of OIMACHI TRACKS have fully launched co-creative urban development in the wider Shinagawa area. To accelerate its real estate turnover business, the company signed a basic agreement with the Itochu Group on a strategic alliance in the real estate field. Major affiliated companies are Lumine Co., Ltd., ATRE Co., Ltd., JR East Urban Development Co., Ltd., JR East Building Co., Ltd., Nippon Hotel Co., Ltd., Sendai Terminal Building Co., Ltd., JR East Building Tech Co., Ltd., and JR East Real Estate Co., Ltd.

entries.89ba7561ed7e6976: This is a reportable segment that, in addition to passenger transport centered on the railway business, develops the travel business, cleaning and maintenance business, station operations business, construction and facility works business, railway vehicle manufacturing business, railway vehicle maintenance business and others. The company's railway business operating area extends mainly across 1 metropolis and 16 prefectures in the Kanto and Tohoku regions, with 1,632 stations and 7,302.2 km of operating kilometers in total, comprising 6,108.0 km of conventional lines and 1,194.2 km of Shinkansen. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥2,045,840 million, the largest of the 3 reportable segments and 2/3 of consolidated operating revenue. Segment profit (operating income) was ¥194,414 million, the number of employees was 53,165, segment assets were ¥7,522,076 million and capital expenditure was ¥423.9 billion, each the largest among the reportable segments. The company explains the reason for the increase in revenue as an increase in railway transport revenue accompanying higher railway use. It revised fares on March 14, 2026, and introduced one-man operation on the Yokohama and Negishi Lines (between Hachioji and Ofuna). For the Tsugaru Line (between Kanita and Mimmaya) and the Kururi Line (between Kururi and Kazusa-Kameyama), where the characteristics of railways are not being fully exercised, it has announced that it will discontinue the railway business in April 2027 after reaching agreement with local governments. The main related companies are JR Bus Kanto Co., Ltd., Tokyo Monorail Co., Ltd., JR East Byu Tourism & Sales Co., Ltd., JR East Environment Access Co., Ltd., JR East Station Service Co., Ltd., Japan Transport Engineering Company and JR East Technology Co., Ltd.

entries.9d96120f04fd9766: Passengers are divided into commuter and non-commuter; for the fiscal year ended March 2026, passenger-kilometers were 65,174,931 thousand passenger-km for commuter and 63,088,814 thousand passenger-km for non-commuter, roughly half and half. Shinkansen revenue is centered on non-commuter travel (passenger transport revenue of ¥592,051 million, of which commuter revenue was ¥25,426 million), while conventional lines in the Kanto area have commuter revenue of ¥395,767 million and non-commuter revenue of ¥768,217 million, a structure with heavy commuter and school use. For inbound foreign visitors, it newly introduced the "JR EAST PASS" and expanded the "JR East-South Hokkaido Rail Pass" to cover Tohoku and Niigata. Railway users are also customers of in-station stores, shopping centers and hotels, and there are also tenant companies in office buildings. Because revenue from external customers in Japan exceeds 90% of revenue, information by region is not disclosed, and there is no counterparty accounting for 10% or more of revenue.

entries.a75a102ffa4c02b5: Consolidated operating revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥3,084,679 million, up 6.8% year on year, with revenue increasing in all segments. Revenue from external customers by segment was ¥2,045,840 million for the Transportation Business, ¥513,227 million for the Real Estate and Hotel Business, ¥416,133 million for the Distribution and Services Business, and ¥109,477 million for Other. Looking at the company's railway business within the Transportation Business, passenger transportation revenue was ¥1,848,537 million (Shinkansen ¥617,477 million, Conventional Lines in the Kanto Area ¥1,163,985 million, Conventional Lines outside the Kanto Area ¥67,074 million), and with railway track usage fee revenue of ¥6,616 million and transportation miscellaneous revenue of ¥165,288 million added, total railway revenue was ¥2,020,442 million. Railway fare revenue is built up with revenue from station stores, shopping centers, office leasing, hotels, real estate sales, and the IC card business. The company and most of its consolidated subsidiaries operate in businesses that do not adopt made-to-order production.

entries.b891b53db4f5928c: A reportable segment operating retail, food and beverage, wholesale, trucking, advertising agency and other businesses. The company is responsible for creating station space. Retail and food and beverage operations are handled by JR East Cross Station Co., Ltd. and JR East Tohoku Sogo Service Co., Ltd., wholesale by JR East Trading Co., Ltd., trucking by JR East Logistics Co., Ltd., and advertising agency by JR East Planning Co., Ltd. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, external customer revenue was ¥416,133 million (up 5.7% year on year), segment profit (operating profit) was ¥68,072 million, the number of employees was 6,310 (excluding 7,660 temporary employees), and segment assets were ¥432,472 million. Capital expenditure was ¥34.9 billion, used for opening new stores and improving existing stores. The company explains the revenue increase as higher sales at in-station stores, and says it promoted the 'Beyond Stations' concept, which aims to transform stations from transport hubs into platforms for daily life that connect people, goods and experiences.

entries.d0d15e05cdf227ad: The transportation business includes the passenger motor vehicle transportation business (JR Bus Kanto Co., Ltd., Tokyo Monorail Co., Ltd.), the travel agency business (JR East Byu Tourism & Sales Co., Ltd., JTB Corp.), the cleaning and maintenance business (JR East Environment Access Co., Ltd.), the station operation business (JR East Station Service Co., Ltd.), the construction and facility works business (Toutetsu Kogyo Co., Ltd., Daiichi Kensetsu Kogyo Co., Ltd., Nippon Densetsu Kogyo Co., Ltd., Nippon Leetec Co., Ltd., Tekken Corporation), the railcar manufacturing business (Sogo Sharyo Seisakusho Co., Ltd.), and the railcar maintenance business (JR East Technology Co., Ltd.). A structure in which group companies handle the construction, cleaning, station operation, and railcar manufacturing and maintenance needed to run trains.
entries.d205dcb591835a66: The company's railway business covers one metropolis and 16 prefectures, 1,632 stations and a route length of 7,302.2 km. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, passengers carried totaled 6,034,303 thousand (commuter 3,487,035 thousand; non-commuter 2,547,267 thousand), passenger-kilometers were 128,263,745 thousand passenger-km, and load factor was 62.5% for the Shinkansen and 43.6% for conventional lines. Overlaid on this are in-station stores, shopping centers, office buildings, hotels, real estate development and sales, and Suica and credit cards. Capital expenditure for the fiscal year ended March 2026 totaled ¥949.1 billion, broken down as follows: Real Estate and Hotel Business ¥454.3 billion, Transportation Business ¥423.9 billion, Other businesses ¥35.8 billion, and Retail and Service Business ¥34.9 billion. Funds for the Transportation Business were used for large-scale earthquake countermeasures, platform screen door installation and new rolling stock, while funds for the Real Estate and Hotel Business were used for construction work on "TAKANAWA GATEWAY CITY", "OIMACHI TRACKS" and "Shibuya Scramble Square". Total R&D expenses were ¥25 billion, and under the "Medium- to Long-Term Vision for Technological Innovation", the company is pursuing development of next-generation Shinkansen using the test vehicle "ALFA-X", walk-through ticket gates, smart maintenance that monitors tracks and power facilities while trains are running, and the hydrogen hybrid train "HYBARI", which uses hydrogen as fuel. Basic research and development is entrusted to the Railway Technical Research Institute, a public interest foundation, and the contribution is ¥5 billion.
